A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work, Fast Training of Sinusoidal Neural Fields via Scaling Initialization. Their complete main texts and Appendices A–F, including equations, tables and figures, support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v2 reports original neural-field experiments in Section 5 and additional neural-dataset, NeRF and differential-equation results in Appendix F.

after.justification: v3 retains these original empirical results, including the quantitative comparisons in Tables 1, 3 and 4 and the appendix analyses and reconstructions.

M1.justification: The architecture and weight-scaling procedure remain unchanged: initialized weights are multiplied by alpha except in the final layer. Equations (1)–(3), training objectives and task-specific adaptations match.

E1.justification: Both versions use Kodak/DIV2K images, Lucy occupancy data, ERA5, Bach audio, MNIST/CIFAR-10 neural datasets, Lego/Drums NeRF scenes and wave-equation reconstruction. No dataset, task or test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains the same nine baselines, including SIREN initialization, NFSL, WIRE and Sinc NF. Comparator membership also matches within the neural-dataset, NeRF and appendix qualitative comparisons.

E3.justification: Splits, preprocessing, sample sizes, metrics, model sizes and training budgets match throughout Section 5 and Appendix F. Both NeRF resolution/epoch combinations and the extended-training protocol are retained.

E4.justification: Both retain the initial-function versus gradient ablation, spectral and eigenvalue analyses, scaling-factor sensitivity, mini-batch experiments, other-activation comparisons and extended-training analysis. Their tested questions and supporting evidence are unchanged.

E5.justification: Both Table 1 captions and Appendix F.4 specify five random seeds and reporting means and standard deviations. Uncertainty reporting in the appendix tables also matches; no statistical procedure or run-count information changes.

E6.justification: Numerical entries, plotted results and qualitative reconstructions match throughout. For example, weight scaling retains Kodak PSNR 42.83±0.35 in Table 1 and Lego test PSNR 28.17 for the 800×800, 300-epoch setting in Table 4.

T1.justification: The mathematical statements, assumptions, equations and proofs remain unchanged, including Appendices A–C. Several references and proof headings change from Proposition or Lemma to Theorem, but the corresponding statement labels and mathematical content are retained.

C1.justification: Both retain the claims of up to tenfold training acceleration, effectiveness across data domains, improved high-frequency representation and better-conditioned optimization. The scope of the claimed contributions is unchanged.

C2.justification: Both retain the speed–generalization interpretation, frequency and conditioning explanations, downstream-classification tradeoffs and qualifications concerning other activations. Section 6 still acknowledges the limited architectural scope and absence of an explicit convergence bound.

D1.justification: v3 adds an abstract statement that code is available, linked to the project repository effl-lab/Fast-Neural-Fields; v2 lacks this project-code link. This adds access information, while implementation descriptions, hyperparameters and hardware disclosures remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The cited works, bibliography and research positioning match. Comparisons with SIREN initialization, NFSL, meta-learning and initialization-scale research are substantively unchanged.

P1.justification: v3 removes the stray word Another at the end of Section 4.2 and changes many Appendix references to Section. Several references and proof headings now say Theorem despite retained Proposition/Lemma statement labels. The narrative and section organization otherwise remain stable.

P2.justification: All 23 figures and four tables retain their graphics, structures and placement. Changes are limited to local text reflow and caption references, notably Appendix F.1 becoming Section F.1 in Figure 2 and Lemma 5 becoming Theorem 5 in Figure 8.

improvement.justification: The new abstract code link improves implementation discoverability, providing a modest documentation benefit over v2. The inconsistent theorem references introduce a small editorial regression, but the numbered statements remain identifiable. Overall, the access improvement is limited and practical; the scientific evidence and conclusions are unchanged.
